newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-ADT would reject $22.50 cash bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ADT would reject $22.50 cash bid.

text.p: ADT Chairman Michael Ashcroft harshly criticzed the latest hostile takeover bid from Western Resources Inc, saying the revised $22.50 per share cash and stock offer was "woefully inadequate."
In a telephone interview, Ashcroft also said ADT's board would reject even an all-cash offer of $22.50 from Western Resources.
"I think all that Western has done today is tinker with what is a woefully inadequate bid. All that Western has done today is rearrange the deck chairs on the Titanic," he said.
Earlier Monday, Western Resources revised its $3.5 billion hostile bid to offer ADT shareholders more cash in the transaction. ADT quickly rejected the latest offer.
"It's just a bad bid that can only get worse. They can't correct the bid by dumping out more equity," Ashcroft said.
Separately, ADT expects to complete the sale of its auto auction business in the second quarter. He confirmed estimates that the unit's value was about $450 million.
Western Resources, which owns 27 percent of ADT, launched the unsolicited offer on December 18.
Western Resources had been widely expected to try to acquire ADT after the collapse of a merger agreement last year between ADT and Republic Industries Inc.
ADT has indicated that it would consider reasonable offers, but Ashcroft declined to comment on whether the company had been approached by another prospective bidder.
Industry experts have said the Western offer for North America's largest electronic security company is too low and have speculated that Western is likely to raise its bid.
But ADT's stock price is trading at less than the level of the offer now on the table.

"I think the market has worked out that it's better to have the certainty of ADT as a pure play than the uncertainty of a Western with its bad financial structure and deregulation," Ashcroft said in explaining the current stock price.
Federal deregulation has prompted U.S. utilities such as Western Resources to expand into new areas.
